MosoFin · duplicate invoice detection, in plain words

Did I pay the same bill twice?

A supplier chases a bill you already paid. Someone enters it again, and the money goes out a second time. This skill reads your bills, your payments, your supplier records and your open credits. It finds the bill that went out twice, before or after the money left.

The 20-second version

You give it a period. It reads every bill and every payment in a wider window, and runs ten tests on them. Each match gets a confidence level and a reason. It lists the unpaid duplicates first, because you can void those at no cost. One test, the bank-account test, cannot run from a MosoFin connection. It runs only when you upload your suppliers' bank details. When it does not run, the skill says so on the result. It never voids a bill, never merges a supplier and never asks a supplier for money.

What a scan finds

One scan of Northbrook Trading: four months of bills

Northbrook reviews September. The skill scans 1 July to 31 October, a wider window, because a duplicate often sits on each side of a month end. It reads 1,284 bills from 212 suppliers, including 9 inactive supplier records, 1,197 payments and 14 open credits. It finds six groups of records that look like the same bill. The skill calls each group a cluster.

The mistakes it catches

"We check each bill when it arrives, so nothing goes out twice"

The usual control is a person who looks at each bill as it comes in. That person sees one bill at a time. A duplicate looks like any other bill, because it is a copy of a real one. The skill compares every bill with every other bill in the window. In this example it finds three things the one-at-a-time check missed.

What the skill does

Every bill against every other bill, and every payment against every bill
Harbor INV-0442, entered on 3 Sep and again on 19 Sep$1,250.00
Crestline INV-7731, paid by cheque on 22 Aug and by ACH on 4 Sep$4,860.00
Pinnacle INV-2210, under two supplier records, one open$3,200.00
Credit note CN-0011, never used$410.00
The skill lists the open Pinnacle bill first. A person voids it before payment, and the $3,200.00 never leaves. For Harbor and Crestline it proposes a recovery: a credit on the next invoice, or a refund.

The common shortcut

Pay each bill as it comes in
Harbor's second copy of INV-0442 looks like a new billpaid
Crestline's reminder gets a second payment by ACHpaid
Pinnacle's open bill waits for its turndue
The $410.00 credit stays with Harborunused
$6,110.00 left twice. $3,200.00 more is about to. Harbor still holds $410.00 of your money.
The same number, twice

Harbor INV-0442, $1,250.00

The same supplier and the same invoice number is the strongest signal the skill has. It flags this match at Very High confidence, even when the dates or the amounts differ a little. Both copies were paid, so $1,250.00 went out twice. The skill proposes a credit on Harbor's next invoice as the first option, and a refund as the second. It also drafts the entry for a person to post.

Two channels, one bill

Crestline INV-7731, $4,860.00

The bill list shows INV-7731 once. The payment list shows it paid twice: a cheque on 22 August and an ACH transfer on 4 September. A search of the bills alone cannot find this. The skill reads the payments as well, with the method of each one. The paper trail, the cancelled cheque and the ACH record, shows both payments. The IRS tells a business to keep such documents in an orderly way, by year and by type4.

One supplier, two records

Pinnacle INV-2210, $3,200.00

Pinnacle Design exists twice in your vendor master, your list of supplier records. INV-2210 sits under each record. One copy was paid and one is still open. The skill reports two findings from one match: a supplier record to merge and a duplicate bill. A person voids the open copy, and the $3,200.00 never leaves. If that copy is in a closed period, the skill proposes a vendor credit in the current period instead. The skill proposes the merge and never does it. In QuickBooks a merge moves the duplicate's history to the record you keep and makes the duplicate inactive. To bring a merged supplier back, you must create its profile again by hand2.

A credit nobody used

Harbor CN-0011, $410.00

Harbor gave Northbrook a credit note on 12 September. Since then Northbrook paid three later Harbor invoices in full. Nobody used the credit. This is not a duplicate. It is $410.00 that Harbor owes Northbrook. The skill reports it on its own at every sensitivity, so it does not hide among the duplicates.

Why the scan runs every month

A false bill can run for a year and a half before anyone sees it

Most duplicates are honest errors. Some are not. A fraud study of 1,921 cases found a billing scheme, false or inflated invoices, in 424 of them, which is 22%1. The skill does not know which kind it found. It reports the cluster, the rule and the confidence, and a person decides.

Median loss$100,000The median loss in a billing scheme, in the same study1
Time to detection18 monthsHow long a billing scheme typically ran before detection, against 12 months for all frauds1
Caught early$30,000Median loss when a fraud was caught within six months. Frauds that ran two to three years had a median loss of $250,0001

The study counts frauds of every kind. It does not say how often a duplicate scan finds one. The skill's own files say to save each cleared cluster between runs. Without that list, the same false alarms return every month and nobody reads the report.

The ten tests

Ten rules, from the surest to the weakest

The skill runs every rule, in this order, and lists every match with its confidence. The confidence level says how strong the evidence for a match is. Your sensitivity setting decides which matches go into the headline exposure and the recovery plan. Standard takes High and Very High, Strict adds Medium, and Permissive takes Very High only. The summary also counts the matches below the setting, with their amount. The skill prints the setting on every result, because a clean result under Permissive means something very different from one under Strict.

RuleWhat it looks forConfidenceRuns here?
1Same supplier, same invoice number. A near-match number at the same amount, such as 1043 and 1043A, counts too, at HighVery HighYes
2Same supplier, same amount, same date, different invoice numbersHighYes
3Same supplier, same amount, dates within 7 days (you can change the window)MediumYes
4Same amount, supplier names that look alike, such as "Acme Corp" and "Acme Corporation"MediumYes
5An invoice number out of sequence, such as one lower than numbers already paidMedium-LowYes
6Same invoice number under two supplier recordsHighYes
7Two supplier records that share one bank account. The fraud test.HighNot from MosoFin. On the upload path, yes, if you upload supplier bank details. Otherwise reported as not run, with an owner.
8Round amounts that repeat in a short window, above a count that you setLowYes
9One bill paid through two channels, such as a cheque and a wireHighYes, when the payment list has the method
10A credit note never used while later bills were paid in fullLowYes. Reported on its own as money owed to you, at every sensitivity

Rule 4 scores how alike two names are, from 0 to 1. The score gives extra weight to names that start the same way3. The skill flags a pair at 0.85 or above and shows the score, so a person can judge it. Acme Corp and Acme Corporation scored 0.91. Rule 3 found Summit Cleaning's $950.00 on 1 September and 6 September, five days apart. It did not flag the 1 October invoice. That bill is outside the 7-day window, and a bill about 30 days later is a monthly pattern, not a duplicate.

One honest limit

A clean scan never means the fraud test passed

Rule 7 looks for two supplier records that pay into one bank account. That is either one supplier entered twice or a fraud set up on purpose. It is the one rule aimed at fraud. MosoFin does not expose supplier bank details, on purpose, because bank details are the main target in payment fraud. So on the MosoFin path the skill cannot run Rule 7, and it reports the rule as not run. It names the person or team who runs the test in your banking or payables system. Northbrook's result says: Rule 7 not run, owner the bank's payments team. The rules-run sheet shows 9 rules ran and 1 did not. On the upload path, you can upload the last four digits of each supplier's account and the routing or sort code. Then Rule 7 runs. The skill masks every account number in the output and never stores them.

Two outside facts show why the skill will not stay quiet about it. In 2024 businesses reported $2,770,151,146 lost to business email compromise, a fraud by email, in 21,442 complaints. A supplier's compromised email account is one way the fraud worked5. The standard control is to keep approving, paying and recording with different people, which helps prevent fraud, waste and abuse6. The skill does not replace either. Each time Rule 7 does not run, the skill tells you that the bank-account test is still yours to run.

How a run starts

It asks six questions before it reads anything

  1. Use MosoFin for this run, or upload the data yourself?
    MosoFin is the connection to your books and the other platforms you link. With it, the skill reads your bills and payments from there. Without it, you upload the files and the ten rules stay the same. The skill asks only if your account has a MosoFin connection.
  2. Which company, or companies? If you run several, should it also scan across them?
    The skill never picks the company for you. One bill paid by two of your companies is invisible to each company's own scan.
  3. Which period should the scan cover, and how far back before it?
    The skill never picks a period for you. It reads a window wider than the month you review, and it states the window that it read. A duplicate often sits on each side of a month end, and a pair across a year end is a known fraud pattern.
  4. Which suppliers bill the same amount on purpose every month: rent, subscriptions, retainers?
    Those are the main source of false alarms. Without your list, the skill filters their repeat bills by the date pattern at Rule 8, not by name.
  5. Strict, Standard or Permissive? And a window for Rule 3, if not 7 days?
    The setting decides which confidence levels count in the headline exposure. The skill still lists every match. Without an answer it uses Standard and 7 days, and prints both on the result.
  6. Do you have results from an earlier scan: clusters you already reviewed and cleared?
    Without them the same false alarms come back every month. The skill scans without them and offers to save the cleared clusters at the end.

The skill's method also asks you for the Rule 8 threshold: how many equal round-number bills from one supplier, in what window. Without one, it lists those clusters for review and says that it applied no threshold. On the MosoFin path it also says, before any result, that Rule 7 is manual and who should run it.

Then it reads your answers back and waits for your yes:

"Scanning Northbrook Trading's bills and payments from 1 July to 31 October. That is a wider window than September, the month under review. I read them from your Mosofin connection, with inactive vendor records included. Sensitivity Standard, Rule 3 window 7 days. The landlord, the insurer and three software suppliers are on the recurring list. Rule 7 cannot run here. It needs your payables or banking system. Shall I go ahead?"
What you need

Connect once, or upload the files yourself

Connected with MosoFin

Say yes to the read-back

  • It reads every bill in the window, page by page to the end, and states the count
  • It reads every payment with its method, for Rule 9
  • It reads direct purchases, card charges and manual journal entries that skipped the bill process
  • It reads your supplier records, inactive ones included
  • It reads your open credit notes, for Rule 10
  • If you run several companies, it asks whether to scan across them. One bill paid by two companies is invisible to each company's own scan
Uploading instead

Bring the bills and the payments

  • Bill and payment list (CSV or XLSX): every bill in the window, voided bills included. Give the supplier, invoice number, date, amount, order reference, payment date, payment method and status. Required
  • Cheques, expenses and card charges by supplier (CSV or XLSX), for the same window: the payments made outside the bill process. Required for Rule 9
  • Supplier records, inactive ones included, with tax IDs and payment addresses. Recommended, the look-alike rules need it
  • Open credit notes and open payables. Recommended, for Rule 10 and for paid against unpaid
  • Supplier bank details: the last four digits and the routing or sort code. Optional, they let Rule 7 run. The skill masks them and never stores them
  • Your recurring-supplier list, sensitivity, Rule 3 window and cleared clusters, typed in the chat
What you get back

Seven sheets: the clusters, the money, and what ran

The summaryThe period, and how many records it scanned against how many exist. The headline exposure by confidence, paid against open, and the sensitivity used. The matches below the setting, with a count and an amount. The Rule 3 window, the Rule 8 threshold and the window that it read.
Every cluster, side by sideEach group of records with its rule, its confidence, the amount per record, the cluster total, the duplicate exposure and the paid status. The records sit next to each other, so a person can agree or dismiss in seconds. Columns beside them hold the reviewer's decision, the reason, the name and the date.
The detailEvery field the skill used to match: the raw and cleaned supplier name and invoice number, the date, the amount, the payment method and date.
Suppliers to mergeEach pair of supplier records that look like one supplier, with the record to keep and the reason. Proposals only.
The recovery planPer cluster, the action and the contact. Unpaid duplicates first, because voiding one costs nothing.
Rules runWhich of the ten rules ran, over how many records, and what each found. Rule 7 appears as not run, with its owner, unless you uploaded bank details. This sheet is what makes "no duplicates found" a statement you can defend.
CoverageFor each task, which tool read the data, how many records it read, and any gap.

It asks whether you want the sheets as an Excel file before it makes one. If you say no, you get the same sheets as tables in the chat.

What it never does
  • Never reads your books without asking. A connected account is not permission.
  • Never reads anything before you answer the six questions and say yes to the read-back.
  • Never voids a record, merges a supplier, or asks a supplier for money. Every action is a proposal for a person.
  • Never picks the period or the company for you. The scan window is wider than the month you review, and the result says how many records it scanned against how many exist.
  • Never reports a rule that did not run as finding nothing. Rule 7 appears as not run, with its owner, whenever it cannot run. The sensitivity setting is on every result.
  • Never saves bank details, bill-level data, or a suspicion attached to a named person. A duplicate is usually an error. It saves cleared clusters and supplier settings, and only when you say yes.
Words you'll hear

Eight terms, in plain English

AP register
The list of supplier bills and what you paid against them. AP is short for accounts payable, what you owe suppliers.
Vendor master
Your list of supplier records. A vendor alias is one supplier that exists under more than one record.
Duplicate payment
The same bill paid twice. The copies can carry the same invoice number, or a changed one, or sit under two supplier records.
Cluster
A group of records that the skill suspects are the same bill. Each cluster carries one rule and one confidence level.
Confidence level
How strong the evidence for a match is, from Very High to Low. Each of the ten rules carries its own level.
Sensitivity
Which confidence levels count in the headline exposure. Strict counts more, Permissive counts less, and Standard sits between. The scan lists every match at every setting, and the result always says which setting ran.
Similarity score
A number from 0 to 1 that says how alike two names are, with extra weight when the first characters agree. The US Census Bureau developed it to match names and addresses between records3. The skill's threshold is 0.85.
Credit note
A document from a supplier that reduces what you owe. One left unused while you pay later bills in full is money the supplier owes you.
Sources

Where the facts on this page come from

The sources are a fraud study, the accounting software's own help and a US statistical method paper. The others are an IRS publication, an FBI report and a US control standard. We checked each one on 27 October 2026 official source pages. We reviewed each linked source on 27 October 2026. Follow the link for the latest wording. What the skill does comes from the skill's own files.

  1. ACFE: Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the NationsBilling schemes, invoices for false or inflated goods or services, appeared in 424 of the 1,921 cases, 22%. The median loss was $100,000. A billing scheme typically ran 18 months before detection, against 12 months for all frauds. Frauds caught within six months had a median loss of $30,000. Those that ran two to three years had a median loss of $250,000.
  2. Intuit: Merge duplicate vendors in QuickBooks OnlineA merge moves the duplicate's past transactions to the vendor you keep and makes the duplicate inactive. To bring a merged vendor back you must create the profile again by hand. Vendors merge in pairs.
  3. US Census Bureau: Overview of Record Linkage and Current Research Directions (Winkler, 2006)The Jaro-Winkler comparator scores how alike two strings are, from 0 to 1, with extra weight when the first characters agree. The Census Bureau developed it to match names and addresses between records.
  4. IRS: Publication 583, Starting a Business and Keeping RecordsPurchases and other transactions create supporting documents such as paid bills, invoices, receipts and cancelled cheques. Keep them in an orderly way, by year and by type. Keep a record that supports an item on a return until the period of limitations for that return ends.
  5. FBI IC3: 2024 Internet Crime ReportVictims reported $2,770,151,146 lost to business email compromise in 2024, across 21,442 complaints. A compromised vendor email account is one of the ways the scheme worked.
  6. GAO: Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government (Green Book), GAO-25-107721When different people hold the authority to approve, the custody of the asset and the accounting, the split helps prevent fraud, waste and abuse.

No outside authority backs the ten rules, their order or their confidence levels. The same is true of the 0.85 threshold, the 7-day window, the three sensitivity settings and the seven sheets. They are the skill's own rules.
